source_name: ASEE — Company contacts (Podgorica office entry)
why_relevant: Confirms a physical ASEE legal entity in Montenegro (Serdara Jola Piletića 3A, Podgorica; cg_office@asseco-see.me), which enables cross-linking to the Montenegro company registry (CRPS) for financials and to public procurement records — an entity-resolution anchor for the competitor map.

source_name: Printec Group — Printec Montenegro country page
why_relevant: Vendor's own Montenegro country page: present since 2014, 15+ staff, transaction-automation focus, works with ME banks. Baseline for the client's own position and, methodologically, the template for how peer vendors present ME footprints.

source_name: Euronet — Montenegro ATM site (euronetatms.me, Serbian/Montenegrin)
source_subtype: vendor local-market site / product & locator pages
why_relevant: Euronet operates an independent ATM estate and ATM-supply business in Montenegro with a dedicated local-language site (products include mobile ATMs for events) and an office at IV Proleterske 26, Podgorica. Direct competitor evidence in the ATM/cash channel, plus a locator of deployed sites.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — newsroom / press releases
why_relevant: Global ATM/branch-automation leader that announces named bank wins including small markets. No Montenegro-specific item surfaced in this pass, but the newsroom (plus its PRNewswire distribution) is the canonical place a ME win would appear and must be standing-monitored.

source_name: NCR Atleos — newsroom / press releases
why_relevant: Post-split ATM-as-a-Service and ATM-hardware vendor actively announcing European market entries (e.g. Portugal, Greece network additions per trade press). A Montenegro deployment or an ATM-as-a-Service deal would be announced here first. No ME item found in this pass.

source_name: Temenos — Customer success stories index
why_relevant: Temenos publishes named core-banking references by bank and country. No Montenegro entry surfaced in this pass, which is itself a competitive signal (ME core banking appears dominated by regional vendors). Worth standing monitoring for any ME or Western Balkans entry.

source_name: OpenWay Group — Way4 case studies
why_relevant: Card-processing platform vendor that publishes detailed named case studies (e.g. Tsesnabank migration from SmartVista to Way4). Competitive-displacement narratives here are the best public evidence of processing-platform switches; monitor for any Western Balkans / ME client.

source_name: BPC (SmartVista) — customer stories / newsroom
why_relevant: SmartVista is a common card/switch platform in SEE; BPC publishes named bank implementations. No ME reference found in this pass — record as monitoring target, not as a confirmed source of ME evidence.

source_name: Halcom — 'List of banks that are using Halcom' support page
why_relevant: A vendor-published, bank-by-bank client list — effectively a free installed-base map for e-banking/digital-signature in the region. If Montenegrin banks appear, it is direct named-client competitor evidence; if not, that absence is itself informative.

source_name: Google Play / App Store vendor-built banking app listings for Montenegro
why_relevant: App package identifiers reveal the vendor behind a Montenegrin bank's digital channel even when neither party issues a press release: 'mne.asseco.android...' (NLB Klik Crna Gora) implies Asseco/ASEE; 'com.payten.nlb.podgorica' (NLB Smart POS Crna Gora) implies Payten. A reliable, continuously updated, hard-to-spin vendor-attribution signal.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom (press) — country-filtered
why_relevant: Scheme press releases routinely name the bank, the enabling vendor and the market when a product launches (the Hipotekarna SoftPOS launch, for example, was co-developed with Mastercard and Visa). Scheme newsrooms often carry a Montenegro announcement that the vendor never publishes.

source_name: Worldline / Ingenico media-relations press releases
why_relevant: Europe's largest acquirer/terminal group; its press releases and divestment notices are the way to detect any ME acquiring or terminal-estate move. No Montenegro-specific item found in this pass; the terminal-supply angle (Ingenico/Verifone hardware behind Payten/Printec estates) makes it worth tracking.

source_name: CBCG procurement documents for the TIPS Clone project (vendor-revealing tenders)
why_relevant: Not a vendor page, but the single best pointer to which international vendors will be named in Montenegro's largest current payments programme (World Bank-financed TIPS Clone / SEPA alignment, Banca d'Italia agreement, target operation mid-2026). Bid documents and award notices surface supplier names before any vendor press release exists.

source_name: Lovćen banka — digital services page (vendor-technology fingerprint)
source_subtype: bank product page used as vendor fingerprint
why_relevant: Bank-side page that names the technology stack a vendor delivered — Apple Pay/Google Pay enablement, PSD2-compliant solution, TIPS Clone instant payments. Useful for reverse-identifying which international vendor/tokenisation partner sits behind each ME bank when the vendor stays silent.

source_name: Bankar.me — vendor recruitment and vendor-announcement coverage
why_relevant: Montenegrin banking trade portal that republishes vendor material — including vendor job ads (e.g. Printec Group hiring an ATM maintenance technician, 2022), which is an indirect but reliable indicator of a vendor's local service footprint and contract wins. Good snowball surface for vendor names absent from English sources.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — vendor deployment trade coverage
why_relevant: Trade outlet that reliably picks up Diebold Nixdorf / NCR Atleos / Euronet deployment and ATM-as-a-Service announcements, often including smaller European markets, and sometimes carries detail the vendor newsroom omits. A safety net for vendor announcements that never reach ME-local media.

source_name: INFINTECH — Western Balkans banking & fintech conference (organised by Logate, Porto Montenegro/Tivat)
why_relevant: The single most on-point source for this cell: the only recurring dedicated banking/fintech conference physically held in Montenegro, run by Montenegrin software vendor Logate. Its sponsor tiers are a literal ranked roster of vendors buying access to ME/WB banks. Observed sponsor list already includes Capsys and 'Green Printec' (Platinum) plus Porto Montenegro (Silver), i.e. direct competitor/partner signal for a Printec-type player.

source_name: INFINTECH speakers directory (bank executive ↔ vendor pairing map)
why_relevant: Named speaker roster with employer and job title — exactly the 'which bank executive is on stage with which vendor' signal the cell rationale calls for. Observed 2026 roster includes OTP Bank Plc (Deputy CEO Digital), George Labs, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine CIO, Moldindconbank head of cards, Bank of Albania director of payment systems, EPI New Markets Lead, PwC SEE, SME Banking Club — i.e. a regional payments-decision-maker directory.

source_name: Logate (INFINTECH organiser) — Montenegrin banking software vendor
why_relevant: Logate is both a local competitor/partner in ME banking software and the conference owner; who it invites, sponsors and co-presents with is a partnership map in itself. Its director Ivica Tatar is quoted as conference organiser in ME press.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (SCMN) — "Montenegro Financial Markets" international conference
why_relevant: Regulator-hosted annual conference (3rd edition Sept 2025, 520+ participants from 24 countries), co-organised with Ministry of Finance and CBCG. Sponsor list is explicitly published — Visa named platinum sponsor — making it a clean read on which payment schemes and vendors are buying institutional proximity in ME.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking trade portal, Konferencije section
why_relevant: Dedicated local-language banking media with a standing 'Konferencije' category — the cheapest way to discover ME banking events that have no standalone website, plus recaps naming sponsors and speakers (e.g. its INFINTECH 2025 coverage). Also carries policy items such as the Fintech Strategy 2025-2029 adoption.

source_name: IT SPOT — Montenegro's technology summit (Podgorica), Sponzori page
why_relevant: 500+ attendee national tech summit with an explicit public sponsors page and Privredna komora Crne Gore as strategic partner. Banks and their IT suppliers routinely sponsor; it is the general-tech complement to INFINTECH's banking focus and surfaces vendors before they appear in banking-specific venues.

source_name: ICT Cortex (Montenegrin ICT cluster) — Events section
why_relevant: Cluster of ME IT companies that both organises and co-sponsors local tech events; its event feed points to conferences, delegations and expos where ME software vendors selling to banks appear, and its membership list doubles as a local-competitor roster.

source_name: Digitalizuj.Me — Montenegrin digital community, event and conference coverage
why_relevant: Long-running (since 2011, 50+ events) local-language digital community portal that announces and recaps ME tech/business conferences including Spark.me and Digital Day; useful for catching small events and named sponsors that never reach English media.

source_name: Spark.me conference (Budva) — general sponsor and partner roster
why_relevant: Montenegro's flagship business/tech conference in Budva (reported ~580 attendees from 28 countries; m:tel as general sponsor). Not banking-specific but its sponsor roster reliably includes ME banks and telcos, showing who is buying visibility and with whom they co-brand.

source_name: Forum izvršnih direktora (FID) — Montenegro CEO forum, sponsor tiers
why_relevant: Annual Podgorica CEO forum (Hilton) whose sponsor tiers are published by name: Mtel diamond, NLB Banka AD Podgorica platinum alongside EPCG, Lognet, Nu Energy. Direct evidence of which banks are spending on executive-level visibility and which local IT firms sit beside them.

source_name: Investitor.me — Montenegrin business/finance portal (event, sponsorship and award coverage)
why_relevant: Reliable local outlet that publishes both conference sponsor rosters (FID) and bank award announcements (e.g. CKB named Bank of the Year in Montenegro). Serves as the discovery layer for ME events and awards in local language.
